drivingQuestion: How are the conflicting tannaitic rulings about asparagus — what it is supplemented with, whom it benefits, and whether one spits after it — to be reconciled?
outcomeNote: All three contradictions are resolved by the single distinction between asparagus of wine and asparagus of beer, and Rav Ashi draws a practical consequence.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּאִסְפָּרָגוֹס: אֵין שׁוֹתִין אוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא חַי וּמָלֵא; מְקַבְּלוֹ בְּיָמִין וְשׁוֹתֵהוּ בִּשְׂמֹאל; וְאֵין מְשִׂיחִין אַחֲרָיו, וְאֵין מַפְסִיקִין בּוֹ; וְאֵין מַחֲזִירִין אוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא לְמִי שֶׁנָּתְנוּ לוֹ; וְרָק אַחֲרָיו; וְאֵין סוֹמְכִין אוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בְּמִינוֹ.
segments.en: «The Sages taught: Six things were said with regard to asparagus: One only drinks it undiluted and» from a «full» cup; «he receives it» from the attendant «in» his «right» hand «and drinks it with» his «left» hand; «one should not converse after» drinking it «and one does not stop» while drinking «it,» but should drink it all at once; «one only returns it to» the one «who gave it to him; and he spits after» drinking «it; and one may only supplement it with its own kind,» meaning that after drinking asparagus, one should only eat something that is used to make similar beverages, e.g., dates after date beer, etc.

segments.he: וְהָתַנְיָא אֵין סוֹמְכִין אוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בְּפַת! לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא — בִּדְחַמְרָא, הָא — בִּדְשִׁכְרָא.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «Wasn’t it taught» in a baraita that «one may only supplement» asparagus «with bread?» The Gemara responds: That is «not difficult. This» baraita«,» in which it was taught that one supplements it with bread, refers to asparagus made «of wine,» while «that» baraita«,» in which it was taught that one supplements it with its own kind, refers to asparagus made «of beer.»

segments.he: תָּנֵי חֲדָא לְלַעַ״ט יָפֶה, לְרָמַ״ת קָשֶׁה. וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: לְרָמַ״ת יָפֶה, לְלַעַ״ט קָשֶׁה! לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא — בִּדְחַמְרָא, הָא — בִּדְשִׁכְרָא.
segments.en: «It was taught» in «one» baraita that asparagus «is beneficial for L-E-T,» heart, eyes, and spleen, «and harmful for R-M-T,» head, intestines, and hemorrhoids. «And it was taught» in «another» baraita that asparagus «is beneficial for R-M-T,» head, intestines, and hemorrhoids, «and harmful for L-E-T,» heart, eyes, and spleen. The Gemara responds: That is «not difficult. This» baraita, in which it was taught that asparagus is beneficial for L-E-T, refers to asparagus made «of wine,» while «that» baraita, in which it was taught that asparagus is harmful for L-E-T, refers to asparagus made «of beer.»

segments.he: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: רָק אַחֲרָיו — לוֹקֶה. וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: לֹא רָק אַחֲרָיו — לוֹקֶה! לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא — בִּדְחַמְרָא, הָא — בִּדְשִׁכְרָא.
segments.en: The Gemara resolves a contradiction between two other baraitot in the same manner. «It was taught» in «one» baraita that «if he spit after» drinking asparagus, he «suffers» an illness. «And it was taught» in «another» baraita that «if he did not spit after» drinking asparagus, he «suffers» an illness. The Gemara responds: That is «not difficult. This» baraita, in which it was taught that if he spit after drinking it he «suffers» an illness, refers to asparagus made «of wine,» while «that» baraita, in which it was taught that if he did not spit he suffers an illness, refers to asparagus made «of beer.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ לֹא רָק אַחֲרָיו לוֹקֶה, מֵימָיו נִזְרָקִין אֲפִילּוּ בִּפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi said: Now» that «you said» that «if he did not spit after» drinking it he «suffers» an illness, «its water,» the saliva in his mouth after drinking asparagus«,» may be expelled «even» when standing «before the king,» as failure to do so will endanger him.
